f: Level 1 Foundation — Theorem 2.1: The Integrating Factor & Product Rule Inversion
f_ar: Level 1 Foundation — Theorem 2.1: The Integrating Factor & Product Rule Inversion
b: Let \( P(x) \) and \( Q(x) \) be continuous on an open interval \( I \). Define the integrating factor: \[ \mu(x) = \exp\left(\int P(x)\,dx\right). \] Then \( \mu(x) > 0 \) for all \( x \in I \), and a function \( y(x) \) is a solution to \( y' + P(x)y = Q(x) \) if and only if \[ y(x) = \frac{1}{\mu(x)}\left(\int \mu(x)Q(x)\,dx + C\right) \] for some constant \( C \in \mathbb{R} \).
b_ar: Let \( P(x) \) and \( Q(x) \) be continuous on an open interval \( I \). Define the integrating factor: \[ \mu(x) = \exp\left(\int P(x)\,dx\right). \] Then \( \mu(x) > 0 \) for all \( x \in I \), and a function \( y(x) \) is a solution to \( y' + P(x)y = Q(x) \) if and only if \[ y(x) = \frac{1}{\mu(x)}\left(\int \mu(x)Q(x)\,dx + C\right) \] for some constant \( C \in \mathbb{R} \).

f: Level 1 Foundation — Theorem 3.1: Superposition Principle & Vector Space of Solutions
f_ar: Level 1 Foundation — Theorem 3.1: Superposition Principle & Vector Space of Solutions
b: Let \( L[y] = a y'' + b y' + c y \) be the linear differential operator. If \( y_1(x) \) and \( y_2(x) \) are solutions to \( L[y] = 0 \) on an open interval \( I \), then any linear combination \[ y(x) = C_1 y_1(x) + C_2 y_2(x), \qquad C_1, C_2 \in \mathbb{R} \] is also a solution. The solution set \( \ker(L) \) forms a two-dimensional vector subspace of \( C^2(I) \).
b_ar: Let \( L[y] = a y'' + b y' + c y \) be the linear differential operator. If \( y_1(x) \) and \( y_2(x) \) are solutions to \( L[y] = 0 \) on an open interval \( I \), then any linear combination \[ y(x) = C_1 y_1(x) + C_2 y_2(x), \qquad C_1, C_2 \in \mathbb{R} \] is also a solution. The solution set \( \ker(L) \) forms a two-dimensional vector subspace of \( C^2(I) \).

f_ar: Level 1 Foundation — Theorem 4.1: General Solution Structure & Affine Subspaces
b: Let \( L[y] = a y'' + b y' + c y \). If \( y_p(x) \) is any fixed particular solution of \( L[y] = g(x) \), then the complete general solution is \[ y(x) = y_c(x) + y_p(x) = C_1 y_1(x) + C_2 y_2(x) + y_p(x), \] where \( \{y_1, y_2\} \) is a fundamental solution set of \( L[y] = 0 \). Geometrically, the solution set is an affine subspace of \( C^2(I) \) formed by shifting \( \ker(L) \) by \( y_p \).
b_ar: Let \( L[y] = a y'' + b y' + c y \). b: Let \( \{y_1, y_2\} \) be a fundamental solution set of \( y'' + P(x)y' + Q(x)y = 0 \) with Wronskian \( W(x) \). A particular solution to the nonhomogeneous equation \( y'' + P(x)y' + Q(x)y = g(x) \) is given by: \[ y_p(x) = -y_1(x)\int \frac{y_2(x)g(x)}{W(x)}\,dx + y_2(x)\int \frac{y_1(x)g(x)}{W(x)}\,dx. \]
b_ar: Let \( \{y_1, y_2\} \) be a fundamental solution set of \( y'' + P(x)y' + Q(x)y = 0 \) with Wronskian \( W(x) \). A particular solution to the nonhomogeneous equation \( y'' + P(x)y' + Q(x)y = g(x) \) is given by: \[ y_p(x) = -y_1(x)\int \frac{y_2(x)g(x)}{W(x)}\,dx + y_2(x)\int \frac{y_1(x)g(x)}{W(x)}\,dx. \]

f: Level 1 Foundation — Definition 9.1: Forward Euler's Method & Discrete Vector Fields
f_ar: Level 1 Foundation — Definition 9.1: Forward Euler's Method & Discrete Vector Fields
b: Consider the initial value problem: \[ \frac{dy}{dt} = f(t, y), \qquad y(t_0) = y_0. \] Discretize the time domain into uniform intervals of step size \( h > 0 \), generating discrete grid points \( t_n = t_0 + n h \). Forward Euler's Method approximates the continuous solution \( y(t_{n+1}) \) by extrapolating along the tangent line evaluated at the beginning of the step: \[ y_{n+1} = y_n + h f(t_n, y_n), \qquad n = 0, 1, 2, \dots \]
b_ar: Consider the initial value problem: \[ \frac{dy}{dt} = f(t, y), \qquad y(t_0) = y_0. \] Discretize the time domain into uniform intervals of step size \( h > 0 \), generating discrete grid points \( t_n = t_0 + n h \). Forward Euler's Method approximates the continuous solution \( y(t_{n+1}) \) by extrapolating along the tangent line evaluated at the beginning of the step: \[ y_{n+1} = y_n + h f(t_n, y_n), \qquad n = 0, 1, 2, \dots \]
